name: Elihoreph
title: Solomon's Scribe
summary: Elihoreph was one of King Solomon's scribes (secretaries) who served in his administration. He was the son of Shisha and brother to Ahijah, and the two brothers served together as scribes at the court. His role illustrates the well-developed bureaucratic structure of Solomon's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as a Scribe under Solomon
keyEvents.description: Elihoreph is mentioned as one of King Solomon's highest officials, where he, together with his brother Ahijah, served as a scribe at the royal court.

keyEvents.title: Part of Solomon's Administration
keyEvents.description: Elihoreph was part of the extensive administrative apparatus that Solomon built up to govern his large kingdom effectively.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Kingdom in its Golden Age
keyEvents.description: During Solomon's reign, Israel experienced a period of great prosperity and peace, and Elihoreph served as an important part of this administration.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Wisdom and Organization
keyEvents.description: Solomon's wisdom was expressed not only in his judgments but also in his ability to organize the kingdom with skilled officials like Elihoreph.
